title: The share market

match.reason: No point in the bank covers the share market or the ASX; the closest, companies and limited liability, is about legal structure rather than how shares are issued and traded.

draft.title: The share market
card: A share is a unit of ownership in a company. People who hold shares are shareholders, and they own a small part of that company.
The Australian Securities Exchange (ASX) is Australia's main share market. A company listed on the ASX has its shares open to buy and sell there.
where a company issues new shares and receives the money. This raises finance for the company, for example to fund growth.
where investors trade shares that already exist. The money goes to the selling investor, not to the company.
draft.remember: New shares raise money for the company. Trading existing shares moves money between investors.

a.q: Which of these is a way a company raises finance on the ASX?
opts: Buying its own shares from investors
One investor selling shares to another
a.why: When a company issues new shares, investors pay the company for them, so it receives finance. When investors trade existing shares, the money goes to the seller, so the company receives nothing.
a.clue: Who receives the money when the shares are first created?

b.q: Priya sells 500 shares in Harbour Foods Ltd on the ASX to another investor. What is the effect on Harbour Foods?
opts: It receives no money from the sale
It receives the money from the sale
It receives a share of the sale price
b.why: This is a trade of existing shares in the secondary market, so the money goes to Priya. Harbour Foods raised its finance when it first issued the shares, and the sale does not change that. Only the owner of the shares changes.
b.clue: Were these shares newly issued or already held?

b.best: It receives no money from the sale

check.summary: No problems found. The card correctly explains the primary and secondary markets, and both questions have one clear right answer that matches the card and the explanations.
